title: AI-Powered Mobile Urban Intelligence Platform Using Public Transport Fleet
description:
• Background Urban public transport buses traverse almost every major road in a city every day. Modern buses are increasingly equipped with multiple cameras covering the front, rear, sides, and passenger cabin. However, these cameras are primarily used for recording incidents and are not leveraged as intelligent sensing platforms. At the same time, city authorities rely on fixed CCTV cameras, manual inspections and citizen complaints to identify road defects, traffic congestion,missing infrastructure and unsafe driving behaviour. This results in delayed response,incomplete situational awareness and inefficient maintenance planning.
• Description Develop an AI-powered onboard and centralized software platform that transforms public transport buses into mobile urban sensing units. The onboard software shall analyse video streams from multiple bus-mounted cameras to detect road defects such as potholes, damaged roads, missing road dividers, missing zebra crossings, damaged or missing traffic signboards,waterlogging and other road hazards. It shall estimate vehicle density through vehicle detection, classification and counting, identify traffic bottlenecks, and detect vulnerable pedestrian situations such as school children crossing roads. During incidents such as hit-and-run or rash driving, the system should detect and track the offending vehicle, extract the registration number with a confidence score, timestamp and GPS location, and securely share alerts with a central command system. The centralized platform shall aggregate information from the entire bus fleet, visualize events on a GIS map, generate congestion heat maps,identify infrastructure deficiencies, analyse origin–destination traffic patterns, estimate route delays and provide actionable insights for transport authorities.
• Expected Solution The solution should provide an edge-AI onboard processing framework integrated with a centralized urban intelligence platform. It should generate reliable alerts, GIS-based dashboards, road condition maps, traffic analytics and incident reports to support proactive road maintenance, improved traffic management, enhanced public safety and evidence-based decision making while minimizing bandwidth through intelligent edge processing.
summary: Innovation (4/5): draws on ai, gis applied to a fitness & sports problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Fitness & Sports. Tech Depth (4/5): centers on gis, infrastructure. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (2/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 20/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: AI-Powered Mobile Urban Intelligence Platform Using Public Transport Fleet

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a system that uses the cameras already mounted on city buses to automatically spot potholes, damaged roads, missing signage, and traffic hazards as buses drive their normal routes, turning an entire bus fleet into a roving city-inspection network.
overview.why_it_matters: Buses already cover nearly every major road daily. Using their existing cameras for infrastructure monitoring is a genuinely clever way to get comprehensive, continuous coverage that fixed cameras and manual inspection can't match.
pain_points: Bus-mounted cameras are used only for incident recording, not as intelligent sensing platforms.
City authorities rely on fixed CCTV, manual inspection, and citizen complaints, causing delayed, incomplete situational awareness.
No system currently leverages the comprehensive daily road coverage buses already provide.
overview.background: Public transport buses cover nearly every major city road daily and are increasingly camera-equipped, but this coverage isn't leveraged for infrastructure/traffic monitoring, which currently relies on slower, less comprehensive methods.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI platform analyzing bus-mounted camera video streams to detect road defects, estimate traffic density, identify bottlenecks, and detect vulnerable pedestrians/hazards, turning buses into mobile urban sensing units.
expected_solution: Road-defect detection (potholes, damage, missing infrastructure) from onboard video.
Vehicle density estimation and traffic bottleneck identification.
Centralized aggregation across the bus fleet for city-wide situational awareness.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: High. Repurposing an existing bus fleet's cameras as a distributed urban sensing network is a genuinely clever, non-obvious application, real technical creativity in the framing alone.
analysis.invention_effort_note: High. Requires real computer vision for multiple distinct detection tasks (road defects, vehicle density, pedestrians) operating on genuinely challenging moving-vehicle video (motion blur, varied angles, weather).

competitive_landscape.note: Genuinely creative application concept, requires solid computer vision expertise applied to a real, challenging video domain (moving vehicle footage).

innovation.note: Genuinely clever repurposing of existing infrastructure (bus cameras) for a new sensing purpose, real conceptual creativity.

invention.note: Multiple distinct computer vision tasks on genuinely challenging moving-vehicle video represent substantial technical breadth.

technical_feasibility.note: Public road-defect and traffic-detection datasets exist; the moving-vehicle video challenge (motion blur, angle variation) is real but manageable with existing techniques.

impact_and_benefits.note: Directly improves infrastructure maintenance responsiveness and traffic safety awareness at genuine city scale.

architecture.note: Multiple CV detection modules feeding a centralized aggregation/dashboard system, well-understood pattern applied to a creative use case.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick, genuinely clever and achievable. Scope to 2-3 of the named detection types (road defects and vehicle density are strong, well-supported starting points) rather than attempting comprehensive coverage of every named capability.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Genuinely creative, non-obvious application concept, repurposing existing bus fleet infrastructure is a smart, resource-efficient approach to city-wide sensing.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Real bus-mounted camera footage has genuine challenges (motion blur, varied lighting, weather, vibration) that clean, static-camera datasets don't fully represent, test against realistically degraded footage.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Test your detection models specifically against motion-blurred, vibration-affected, or varied-lighting footage (simulate these conditions if you can't source real bus-mounted footage) rather than only clean, static test images.

idea_0_4: Choose 2-3 detection capabilities to build well (road defects and vehicle density/bottleneck detection are strong starting points).
Source public road-defect and traffic-detection datasets, and if possible, footage with realistic motion/vibration characteristics.
Split: one person on road-defect detection, one on vehicle-density/traffic analysis.
prototype_4_22: Build your road-defect detection model (potholes, damage, missing infrastructure).
Build your vehicle density/traffic bottleneck detection.
Test both against realistically degraded footage (motion blur, varied angle) if possible.
integration_22_30: Connect detection outputs into a centralized aggregation dashboard.
Test with a genuinely challenging footage sample (simulated bus-camera-style motion) to confirm robustness.
Add basic geospatial tagging of detected issues along the bus route.
polish_30_36: Build a clear city-wide dashboard showing aggregated, geotagged detected issues.
Rehearse a live demo processing footage and showing detected road defects/traffic patterns.
Prepare to discuss how your models handle real-world footage challenges (motion, lighting).
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Test your system live on genuinely challenging, degraded-quality footage (motion blur, poor lighting) rather than clean test images, and show it still detects real issues correctly, that robustness against real bus-camera conditions is what separates this from a lab-condition demo.

strengths: Genuinely creative, resource-efficient application concept using existing infrastructure.
Public datasets exist for the core detection tasks.
weaknesses: Real bus-mounted footage has genuine quality challenges (motion, vibration) that clean datasets don't fully represent.
Full coverage of all named detection types isn't achievable in 36 hours, requires deliberate scoping.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: CV-heavy, with real attention to testing against realistically degraded footage.
team_fit.approach: Source or simulate realistically challenging footage (motion blur, vibration) early, this is what separates a genuinely robust system from a clean-condition demo.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Standard object-detection model architectures for road defects, vehicles, and pedestrians.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Understanding the specific challenges of moving-vehicle-mounted camera footage (motion blur, vibration, angle variation) and designing preprocessing/robustness measures for it.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: A model tested only against clean, static-camera imagery would likely fail against real bus-mounted footage's genuine motion and vibration challenges, exactly the gap between demo and real deployment.

data_resource_availability.status: Public road-defect and traffic-detection datasets genuinely exist; realistic bus-mounted-camera-style footage (with motion/vibration) is harder to source but can be approximated.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: If real bus-mounted footage isn't available, apply realistic motion blur and vibration simulation to clean test footage to approximate real-world conditions, and be clear this is simulated degradation.

judge_qna.question: How does your system handle the real motion blur and vibration of an actual bus-mounted camera, not clean test footage?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Show your results on realistically degraded footage specifically, and describe any preprocessing/robustness measures you built to handle this, being honest about performance differences versus clean footage.
judge_qna.follow_up: What's your detection accuracy drop-off between clean and degraded footage?

judge_qna.question: How would this actually integrate with existing city infrastructure maintenance workflows?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe a realistic reporting/ticketing integration, detected issues should feed into an actionable maintenance queue, not just a passive dashboard.
judge_qna.follow_up: How would you prioritize which detected issues get addressed first at city scale?
